A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same State Delta Encoding (SDE) work. Their complete main texts, equations, six tables, five figures, and Appendices A-D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original SDE evaluations on information-asymmetry, multi-agent debate, and agent-workflow tasks, together with ablations and layer-selection experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results in Tables 1-6 and Figures 2-5, including the appendix experiments.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same token-wise hidden-state differences and their additive injection into the receiving agent. Equations (1)-(3), the layer-selection procedure, and the selected layers in Appendix A are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use Quasar-T, ComplexWebQuestions, and StrategyQA for information-asymmetry tasks; GSM8K and three MMLU subjects for debates; and HotpotQA, StrategyQA, and FEVER for workflows. The 2WikiMultihopQA layer-selection task is also retained.

E2.justification: Single, Natural Language, and CIPHER retain the same participation in the reported comparisons. The single-agent baseline explained in v2 Section 4.1 already appears in v1 Appendix B.1. V2 explicitly discusses an unevaluated full-information baseline without adding it.

E3.justification: Sample sizes, passage allocation, metrics, models, selected layers, generation limits, and agent/round counts remain unchanged. V2 explains the implementation of CIPHER's existing temperature-zero setting and the existing per-agent temperature formula; it does not report a revised protocol.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same layer-selection sensitivity analyses, original-hidden-state ablation, and agent/round-count comparisons in Sections 5.2-5.4 and Appendix C. The added explanatory passages introduce no new analysis results.

E5.justification: Table 2 and Appendix B.2.1 retain averaging over three independent debate runs. Neither version supplies confidence intervals, formal significance tests, or additional seed and variability reporting.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1-6 and plotted results in Figures 2-5 are unchanged. For example, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with SDE retains 0.5198 on Formal Logic debates and 0.3833 on StrategyQA workflows. No result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: The state-trajectory definition, state-delta definition, and injection equation remain unchanged. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs. V2's layer-selection qualifications concern empirical interpretation rather than revised formal assumptions.

C1.justification: The central SDE contribution, single-base-LLM scope, and claims of improved communication and complex reasoning remain unchanged, including the up-to-17.3% improvement claim. V2 makes the single-base-model scope explicit in the abstract, consistent with v1's introduction and methodology.

C2.justification: Sections 3 and 4.5 replace broad claims about task-agnostic, model-determined optimal layers with the qualification that selected layers need not be optimal and generalize across the tested tasks. Section 4.1 and Appendix B.1 acknowledge possible information overlap, interpret baseline gaps as evidence of complementary knowledge, and explain omitting a single agent with all retrieved passages.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 newly explains that CIPHER's nominal temperature zero applies softmax to raw logits, effectively temperature one, and adds a link to the relevant implementation. Appendix B.2.1 explains the rationale for the existing agent-specific temperatures. Hardware, prompts, selected layers, and the paper's code/data access statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography is unchanged, but Section 2.2 revises the comparison with Ramesh and Li (2025). It removes the assertion that their approach cannot support interactive exchanges and instead contrasts their heterogeneous-model debate setting with SDE's multiple instances of the same model.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted edits to the abstract, related-work discussion, layer-selection explanations, and experimental documentation, and adds acknowledgments. The section sequence and Appendices A-D remain intact; there is no extensive narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: Table 5 moves from PDF page 8 to page 9, accompanying text and appendix material reflow, and printed page numbers disappear. The figures, table structures, captions, axes, and legends otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility documentation by explaining CIPHER's temperature handling and improves claim calibration by qualifying layer optimality and generalization. The information-overlap and omitted-control disclosures also clarify the evaluation's scope. The added argument that baseline gaps establish necessary information exchange receives no additional control, so the gains remain limited to clearer documentation and interpretation of unchanged evidence.
